name: clickables
architecture: gradient-boosted trees over the 552 neighbourhood features (176 trees, up to 31 leaves each), temperature-calibrated

data.note: Stand-in corpus: real, hand-written websites from 25 public GitHub repositories (pinned commits, listed in ml/corpus/sources.json), served locally and crawled with the same two-pass labeller as the Tranco plan, because the public web was not reachable from the build machine. Mostly small vanilla-JavaScript projects and reference examples; React and admin-template sites are rare. Pages with document-level click listeners were left out because their labels cannot be trusted. Retrain on the Tranco crawl before trusting it on production sites.

comparisons.model: Rule: pointer cursor and not native

seeds.note: test PR-AUC of the graph network trained with each seed; the shipped seed was chosen on calibration sites

latency.target: <= 50 ms for 2,000 elements in the Web Worker
latency.note: median of 10 runs in the app's Web Worker; headless Chromium, 2 × Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.10GHz, no CPU throttling

beats_best_gbt.target: the graph network beats the best gradient-boosting baseline and passes the gate
beats_best_gbt.note: the graph network missed the gate, so the baseline itself is shipped as the spec's fallback

latency.target: <= 50 ms for 2,000 elements in the Web Worker
latency.note: median of 10 runs in the app's Web Worker; headless Chromium, 2 × Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.10GHz, no CPU throttling

failurePatterns: Images in a product or brand grid with a pointer cursor are flagged although nothing handles their clicks (all 5 false positives were product images on one shop page).
Game boards are missed: chess squares and similar grids of plain divs with no pointer cursor and no button-like class names scored just under the threshold (0.48 against 0.51).
Cards whose only content is an image, like the rock, paper and scissors choices, are missed: there is no text or class word to go on.

Some misses are not really controls: the crawler labels a container as clickable when it carries one listener for its children (an FAQ wrapper, a list, a <main>). These are label noise of the delegation kind, at container level.
A div with an inline onclick but no pointer cursor and no button-like class ("Search User") was missed: the model leans on the cursor and on class words.
limitations: It was trained on a stand-in corpus of hobby and teaching projects from GitHub, not on the planned Tranco crawl of popular sites. Treat it as a demonstration until it is retrained on the Tranco crawl.
React, Vue and Angular pages are almost absent from the training data (a handful of pages), so it has not been measured on framework-built sites.
The test websites hold 94 click-only controls, most of them on a few sites, so every percentage on this page has a wide margin; the 95% intervals are shown where they were measured.
The model in use is the gradient-boosting baseline: the graph network missed the ship gate. Its scores still come from the same 552 cues and the same calibration.

labelProbe.method: Random sample of labelled candidates; each clicked once at its centre in the live page. "responds": the DOM, address or a dialog changed within 400 ms. Skipped as untestable: pages that change by themselves, and elements whose centre is a link or button. A response can still come from a handler on an ancestor, so disagreement is an upper bound on label noise.
labelProbe.reading: Read by hand: the 12 disagreements on pages used for training are 5 hover-effect squares (moving the mouse to click recolours them), 4 countdown timers that tick every second, 1 list item whose content is a button, and 2 unclear (a 'Blog' paragraph and an icon image). None is clearly a click-only control the labeller missed, so the probe's rate is a loose upper bound.
